extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, copyeditors, and typesetters in book and journal publishing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for copyediting and preparing manuscripts to Chicago Manual of Style conventions (capitalization, punctuation, typography, references, tables/figures, and related production rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization (general rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of capitals and lower case (how indicated; rules 1–57), including many exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when to capitalize principal words in titles, proper nouns, first words in sentences, feast days, historical epochs, governmental departments, institutions, and many specific classes (see enumerated list). See sections 1–57 and word-lists (word-lists of exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitalization of specific categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization rules for many categories: books of the Bible, Biblical terms, botanical and zoological names, historical epochs/events, movements, organizations, titles, ranks, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives category-by-category instructions (e.g., capitalization of names of bodies of solar system, regiments, ecclesiastical orders, governmental departments, names of events, names of people/epithets when used as proper names).

rubrics_metrics.name: Italics (use and rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of italics (defined; how indicated) and when to use or avoid italics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use italics for titles of books and other works, words from foreign languages, emphasis, names of genera/species, letters used as letters, symbols for subdivisions, titles after signatures, and more. Notes exceptions (need not be used in lengthy bibliographies). See sections 58–73.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphens and compound-words
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for hyphenation and for hyphenated compounds, including division rules and lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers hyphen use and hyphenated compounds (rules 182–214), lists of hyphenated words, when not to divide hyphenated words, compounds with prefixes (co-, pre-, re-, non-, semi-, demi-, bi-, etc.), and use of hyphen to indicate omitted elements in compounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of words (word breaks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and systems for dividing words at line breaks and general avoidance of unnecessary division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises on systems of division, avoidance of division on two letters, not dividing on letters 'c', 'g', 'j', etc., foreign-language division, and rules for placing divisional mark. See sections 215–31.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comma: general rules and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and extensive rules for use of the comma (omission/insertion contexts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies comma use between adjectives, before and, or, nor; after digits for thousands; omission between consecutive pages; with various clause types (adverbial, appositional, antithetical, participial, parenthetical); with conjunctions and connective particles; to indicate omissions; to separate identical words; extensive rules 141–62.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colons: use and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and illustrations of colon use and rules for a range of functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use after salutatory phrases in letters, between place of publication and publisher, to introduce extracts/statements/lists, to emphasize close connection between clauses, to separate chapter and verse in Scripture passages, to separate volume and page references, and more. See sections 131–36.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dashes (em/en and rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions, sizes, and rules for dash usage in punctuation and typesetting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines em and en dash; uses of dash to denote breaks, transitions, emphasis, to precede summarizing clauses, to connect numbers, to indicate omitted words implied at the beginning of successive paragraphs, and other punctuation functions. See sections 166–75 and examples (261).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellipses
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for the use of ellipses, including treatment in quotations and to indicate omissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ellipses are treated as part of a quotation; rules for spacing and use are given; use of ellipsis to indicate omissions and interaction with punctuation. See sections 180–81 and related notes (88).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation punctuation and extracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for punctuation of quotations and extracts, and treatment of short/long quotations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers punctuation and reduction of quotations, punctuation of extracts, treatment of passages quoted in author's own words, and rules for brief quotations (see sections 73–87, 112).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles of works (formatting and capitalization)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format and capitalize titles of books, essays, chapters, articles, periodicals, lectures, and other works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capitalization of principal words, use of roman type or italics depending on format (e.g., titles of books italicized; titles of essays/cycles/lectures roman-quoted and italicized per rules), treatment of articles in newspaper titles (not part of title), and exceptions per publication type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations (use, spacing, periods)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules about where and how to use abbreviations (literary references, academic degrees, biblical books, directions, states, technical terms, titles of publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies no space between elements of some abbreviations, not to divide abbreviations, omission of period after some abbreviations, use/omission of apostrophe in certain abbreviations, and full lists of standard abbreviations. See referenced sections (e.g., 52, 103, 123, 237).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers and numerals (use and spelling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for when to spell out numbers, when to use figures, treatment of consecutive numbers, round numbers, and numbers in groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spell out numbers commencing a sentence and numbers of less than three digits in ordinary text; set groups of six or more closely connected in figures; treatment of consecutive numbers, use of comma for thousands, dash for 'to' connecting ranges, and related spacing. See sections 94–98, 159, 173.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates (format and punctuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for formatting dates, repetition of hundreds, omission of st/nd/rd/th, comma use between month and year, and dates in bibliographic citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when to repeat hundreds, omit ordinal suffixes, include comma between month and year, place publication dates after volume numbers in periodical references, and other bibliographic date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes (style and numbering)
rubrics_metrics.description: General style for footnotes, numbering, placing of index figure, and exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers general style (sections 232–39), numbering sequences for footnotes, placing the index figure, indexes for references, and samples of footnotes; notes exceptions for some journals and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliographic citations and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for ordering elements in bibliographic citations (authors, titles, volume, page, date), abbreviation conventions, and punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes order of date and volume in periodical references, reduction of citations, use of ibid., loc. cit., op. cit., and when to set certain citation elements in roman or italics (see sections 231–39 and 61).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and alphabetizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for alphabetizing names, indexing conventions, treatment of prefixes/particles, and style for cross-references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how to alphabetize names (rules at 240), treatment of particles (van, von, de), use of 'See' and 'See also' italicization in cross-references, and sizes/type/style for setting indexes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings and headlines (setting and punctuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and rules for setting headings, headline punctuation (period omission), and spacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines center-heads, cut-in heads, box-heads, and rules for omission of period after headlines, spacing of headlines, use of italics for 'continued', and word 'continued' set in italics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tables: alignment, leaders, rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for setting tables: alignment of columns, spacing, use of leaders and double rules, and treatment of figures in columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on alignment in columns (decimals, dollar signs), use of leaders for blanks in ruled columns, double rules in tables, spacing of columns of figures, and sample specimen tables (sections 245–50).

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and illustrations (treatment in text)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for figures (illustrations) in text and letters referring to parts of illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies letters referring to parts of diagrams and illustrations, legends (period omission), and how letters referring to figures should be set (see sections 68, 93).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typography: spacing, em/en quads, hair-space
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed typographic spacing rules (em/en quads, hair-space, even spacing, hair-spacing tabooed, justification, leading, kern).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines em quad, en quad, five-em/four-em space, hair-space; sets rules for even spacing of text, 'justification' defined and rules, leading (leaded), kern, and other typesetting practices (sections 261–77).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotation marks and ironic/ironical use
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of quotation marks for ironic words/phrases and punctuation treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotation marks used to indicate irony; exclamation point may also indicate irony; treatment of words quoted as equivalents or technical terms; see related punctuation rules (section ~77 and 127).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentheses, brackets, and interpolations
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for use of parentheses and brackets, including interpolations and explanatory material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use brackets for interpolations and explanations, rules for parentheses in enumerations and subdivisions, and use of brackets for omitted material or explanatory insertions (sections 176–79, 178).

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation of clauses (adverbial, appositional, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific punctuation rules for clause types: adverbial, antithetical, appositional, complementary, conjunctive, parenthetical, participial, summarizing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives clause-by-clause punctuation guidance (where to use commas, dashes, parentheses), with section references (148–70).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of italics for emphasis and importance
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for using italics to indicate emphasis and importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Italics may be used for emphasis, initial words set in italics in certain contexts, and 'importance' expressed via italics per rules (section 58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of small capitals and capitals/special faces
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for small caps, bold-face type, and indication of typefaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines bold-face type and how it's indicated; rules for capital and small-cap use; how to indicate capitals in specimens and typography sections (sections 50–51, 255).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations: academic degrees and titles
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rules for abbreviation and capitalization of academic degrees, titles, and civil/military/official titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers abbreviation and capitalization of degrees (sections 21–22), treatment of civil and military titles, honorary titles, and capitalization of offices and officers (sections 12, 21, 49).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of apostrophe
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for forming possessives, marking omissions, forming plurals of numerals, and in contractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for use of apostrophe to form possessives, to mark omissions in figures or letters, to form plurals of numerals and of artificial noun-formations, and exceptions (sections 163–65 and 1236 notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign languages and words
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle foreign words/phrases: italicize, provide English equivalent in quotes, division rules, and quoting sentences/passages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Words and phrases from foreign languages set in italics; English equivalents to be quoted; division of foreign words follows particular rules; treatment of quoted foreign sentences addressed in sections 59, 78, 85.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names and indexing rules (particles and prefixes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of personal and place names in indexing, capitalization of particles, and rules for alphabetization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules for Dutch particles (Van, Ten), treatment of 'Mac/Me/M' prefixes, capitalization of familiar names, alphabetization rules and exceptions; see indexing rules (240).

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations in literary references and periodicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Special practices for abbreviations, punctuation, and formatting in literary references and periodical citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists phrases and abbreviations used in literary references (61), exceptions for certain journals (e.g., Botanical Gazette), and notes on punctuation, metric symbols, and footnote style per journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers in tables and figures (alignment & formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to set and align numbers and decimals in tables and columns (spacing and leaders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for aligning decimals and dollar signs, spacing of columns of figures, use of period leader for decimal point, and treatment of columns with averages/generalizations (sections 244–50).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical and algebraic formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: Formatting rules for algebraic formulas and mathematical signs (italics, spacing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use italics for letters designating unknowns, spacing rules for formulas and mathematical signs (section 67, 273), and conventions for geometry lettering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units, measures, and metric symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: How to denote units of measurement, metric symbols, and spacing conventions across contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate units with lower-case initial; spacing rules for metric symbols and hundreds/thousands; treatment of monetary symbols and different-country money notation (sections 94, 123, 270).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinal and Roman/Arabic numerals usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on Roman vs Arabic numerals, spacing, omission of period after Roman numerals, and when to spell out numbers/centuries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for spacing of numerals at line beginnings and headlines, omission of periods after numerals, spelling out centuries and decades, and special treatment for round numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation of parenthetical and appositional clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules specifically for punctuating parenthetical and appositional clauses (commas, dashes, parentheses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States where to use parentheses, commas, or dashes for parenthetical and appositional clauses (sections 150, 167–69).

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles and forms of legal/juridical acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitalization and formatting of acts, laws, bills, and juridical documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for capitalization of names of juridical acts, bills, treaties, and legal documents; treatment of titles of legal causes and proceedings (sections 18, 63).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of punctuation to indicate omission or emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques using comma, dash, ellipsis, and exclamation to indicate omissions, emphasis, or ironic tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comma to indicate omissions in some contexts, dash to indicate implication/omission of words, ellipsis to mark omitted material in quotations, exclamation for emphasis or irony (sections 155, 171, 180, 127).

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic elements: font, face, and specimen rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and guidance for typographic elements (font, face, hairline, brass rule faces, borders, ornaments).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains typographic specimen listings (brass rule faces, hairline/dotted faces, borders of specified point sizes), definition of face, font, kern, and specimen usage for press output.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headwords and index cross-reference style
rubrics_metrics.description: How to format headwords and cross-references in indexes (italicizing 'See' / 'See also', use of small caps).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for italicizing 'See' and 'See also' in cross-references, use of small caps for 'Note' markers, sequence rules for index entries and index figure placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of foreign-script typographic features (ligatures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of ligatures (ae and oe forms), treatment in Latin and other languages, and whether to retain accents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides use of ligatures ‹æ› and ‹œ› (non-use in Latin), retention of accents in foreign words incorporated into English, and division rules for Greek/Latin words.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for headings/lead-ins (box-heads, cut-in heads, center-heads)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and setting rules for various heading types: box-heads, cut-in heads, center-heads, and their punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines these head types, how to set them (capitalization of principal words), omission of period after, and illustration references (sections 279–83).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of personal names and titles in running text and signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for spelling and capitalization of Christian names, family names, and how to handle signatures and author names in articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Christian names to be spelled out; do not repeat author's name in footnotes if in text; omit period after signatures in certain contexts; treatment of titles following signatures to be italicized (sections 93, 161, 65).
